description: An evaluator where a Bomb node explodes if evaluated. Cond evaluates its condition then chooses exactly one branch with a ternary, so the untaken Bomb never detonates.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Imports `dataclass` and `Any` for the AST node definitions.

Four AST nodes: `Num` holds a float value. `BinOp` holds an operator string and left/right children. `Cond` holds condition, then-branch, and else-branch. `Bomb` is empty  -  evaluating it raises `RuntimeError`.
`truthy(v)` implements Python-style truthiness: booleans return themselves, numbers are true if nonzero, everything else is true unless `None`.

`evaluate` dispatches on node type. `Num` returns its value. `bool` returns itself. `Bomb` raises immediately. `Cond` evaluates the condition, then line 26 uses a Python ternary to pick exactly one branch: `evaluate(node.then_ if truthy(cond_val) else node.else_, env)`. This is the non-strict key  -  only the chosen branch is evaluated.
`BinOp` evaluates both children first (strict), then applies the operator via a dictionary of lambdas. This contrast shows strict vs non-strict evaluation in the same interpreter.

steps.answer: The condition evaluates to `False`. The ternary picks `node.else_` (the `Num(42)`). `evaluate` is called on `Num(42)`, returning `42`. The `Bomb` is never passed to `evaluate`, so it never explodes. The print shows `false -> else: 42`.
steps.question: Test 1 creates `Cond(False, Bomb(), Num(42))`. The condition is `False`, so the else-branch `Num(42)` should run. The then-branch is a `Bomb`. What happens?

steps.description: Test 2: `Cond(True, Num(99), Bomb())`. Condition is `True`, so the ternary picks `node.then_` (`Num(99)`). The else-branch `Bomb` is skipped. Print shows `true -> then: 99`.
Test 3: `Cond(Num(0), Num(1), Num(2))`. Both branches are safe `Num` nodes. `Num(0)` is falsy, so the else-branch `Num(2)` runs. Print shows `0 -> else: 2`.
Condition `False` is a `bool`, so line 21 returns `False` directly.
Line 26: `truthy(False)` returns `False`, so ternary picks `node.else_` (the `Num(42)`). `evaluate(Num(42), {})` runs.
`Num(42)` matches line 20, returns `42`. The `Bomb` was never evaluated.
Test 2: `evaluate(Cond(True, Num(99), Bomb()), {})`. Condition `True` picks `node.then_` (`Num(99)`), returns `99`. The else-branch `Bomb` is skipped. Prints `true -> then: 99`.

Test 3: `evaluate(Cond(Num(0), Num(1), Num(2)), {})`. Condition `Num(0)` evaluates to `0.0`. `truthy(0.0)` is `False`, so else-branch `Num(2)` runs. Prints `0 -> else: 2`. All three tests pass without any explosion.

title: Proving If Is Non-Strict With a Bomb Node
